canonical_question: How does the 12 Å by 12 Å cell size compare to the interatomic spacing in the BCC lattice, and could it artificially smooth out composition gradients?

question_variants.question: How does the 12 Å by 12 Å cell size compare to the interatomic spacing in the BCC lattice, and could it artificially smooth out composition gradients?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text mentions the use of 12 Å by 12 Å cells for calculating average concentration but does not compare this size to the interatomic spacing of the BCC lattice, nor does it discuss potential smoothing of composition gradients.

answers.answer: The text states that the system was subdivided into 2D cells of 12 Å by 12 Å to calculate average concentration, but provides no comparison to interatomic spacing or analysis of smoothing effects.
answers.conditions: Cluster expansion and Monte Carlo simulation
answers.measurement_outcome: Average concentration calculated in 12 Å x 12 Å cells.
answers.boundary_limitation: No discussion of lattice spacing comparison or gradient smoothing.
evidence_spans: we have systematically carried out first-principles calculations of phase stability and chemical short-range order (SRO) of the multicomponent 38 at % W/36 at % Ta/15 at % Cr/11 at % V alloy as a function of temperature.
The enthalpies of mixing were calculated using the density functional theory (DFT) and CE methods for nearly 270 structures within the BCC underlying crystalline lattice.

In agreement with previous DFT/CE studies for W-Ta and W-V systems ( [33] ), it is found that the enthalpies of mixing for these two binaries are negative for the whole compositional range, a trend followed also by the Cr-V binary.

source_evidence_spans: we have subdivided the system in 2D cells of 12 Å by 12 Å and calculated the average concentration in every cell.
